text: Ken lit the lantern and stepped into the cellar. He counted the barrels twice.
Mira Voss unrolled the map on the table. She tapped the river crossing and frowned.
Bram shut the gate behind the cart. Then he whistled for the dogs.
Orla poured the tea. She slid a cup across to the guest.
Dorn Hask waited at the bridge until dusk. He never saw the courier arrive.
Yara found the letter under the door. She read it twice before burning it.
Pell dropped the bucket into the well. It hit water with a hollow slap, and he winced.
Hollis shouted across the yard to the stable hands. He wanted the horses ready by dawn.
Ilse sharpened her knife by the fire. She had not spoken since supper.
Tobbin carried the sack of seed to the barn. He stacked it with the others.
Sunnia checked the traps along the ridge. She found two empty and one sprung.
Garrick Tull led the mule up the pass. He whispered to it the whole way.
Ken met Bram at the docks. He had brought the payment in a leather purse.
Bram argued with Ken about the route. He insisted on the mountain road, and Ken gave way.
Mira Voss handed the key to Orla. She would not need it again.
Orla thanked Yara for the warning. She had been following the carriage for hours.
Dorn Hask told Pell the vault was empty. He did not believe it.
Hollis lent Tobbin his cloak. He was shivering by then.
Ilse and Sunnia split the last bread. She ate hers slowly, watching the door.
Garrick Tull and Ken crossed the field at noon. He carried the banner.
Veyra asked Mira Voss to guard the door. She went to fetch the healer.
Bram sold the ring to Hollis. He had never seen one so bright.
Pell and Dorn Hask rowed to the island. He tied the boat to a dead tree.
Yara teased Ilse about the singing. She laughed anyway.
King Aldous Reeve rode in at sunset. The king dismounted without a word.
Ken knelt before Lady Maren Quill. The lady raised him up and asked about the harvest.
The innkeeper, Tobbin, was wiping the bar. The innkeeper nodded toward the back room.
Captain Sunnia reported to the council. The captain left the maps behind.
Aldous Reeve sat on the high seat at the hall. Kesh Arn swore an oath to his king.
Old Pell tended the forge. His apprentice Yara kept the bellows going, and the smith said little.
The priestess Veyra blessed the road. Ken thanked the priestess and walked on.
Hollis Crane, the baron, argued with Garrick Tull all night. The baron finally signed.
Orla has a brother named Bram. Orla visited her brother every spring.
Dorn Hask's sister, Ilse, lives upriver. He sent word to his sister before the thaw.
Ken went to meet his sister at the lake. She had not written in a year.
A hooded figure watched the tavern from the alley. He left when the lamps went out.
Kesh Arn found a letter signed only by the old king. The king asked for help.
The merchant scowled at Yara across the stall. He refused every price she named.
A beautiful elf archer with long blue hair stood on the wall. She never looked down.
Bram heard a stranger humming in the stable. The man stopped as soon as Bram came near.
Ilse stopped at the edge of the marsh. Her mother had told her never to cross it.
A soldier ran past with a message for the captain. He did not stop to be asked.
Mira Voss bought bread from a baker near the gate. The woman wrapped it in cloth and smiled.
Pell stood very still while a pale boy talked. He stared at the ground the entire time.
Ken is the youngest of the guild. Mira Voss, Orla and Bram run it. Yesterday he asked for a vote.
Hollis hired Tobbin to guard the cart. Tobbin brought his own spear, but he had never fought.
Veyra and Garrick Tull argued over the relic. In the end she took it, and he let her.
Sunnia spoke with Ilse and a tall stranger in a grey coat. He gave no name.
Dorn Hask said Pell had lied. He would say it again in front of the council.
Yara watched Ken leave. Later, someone said he had been seen near the old mill, though no one could say who.
Orla and Yara waited by the stairs. She heard footsteps first.
Bram passed Pell the torch at the cave mouth. He took the left tunnel.
